content.title: LDS Church unveils major changes to its Sunday worship services
content.text: No, the two-hour block isn’t getting longer. But the new schedule means shorter classes.(The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints) The global faith is changing its Sunday worship schedule.About 7½ years after The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints did a major overhaul of its Sunday worship schedule, the global faith is at it again.By the fall, members will be attending the same classes — just more frequently and with shorter lessons. The Utah-based faith announced Monday evening that, starting in September, its Sunday block (which was trimmed from three hours to two in 2019) will feature all of its traditional classes for adults and youths every week, rather than every other week. Report Ad[See how Latter-day Saints are reacting to the Sunday meeting changes.]“There is additive strength that comes when we meet each week to counsel, learn and support one another,” said President Camille N. Johnson, who oversees the worldwide women’s Relief Society. “When we gather in his name, the Spirit is there to teach us, testimonies are strengthened, and we lift each other in discipleship. This weekly time for connection will help us draw closer to the Savior and each other.”Here is how it will break down: • 60 minutes: Sacrament meeting, the faith’s primary worship service. Get Mormon Land newsletter. Explore the news and culture of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints every Thursday.• 5 minutes: Transition to classes.• 55 minutes: Children’s primary. • 25 minutes: Sunday school for adults and teens. Report Ad• 5 minutes: Transition to next classes and quorum meetings.• 25 minutes: All-male priesthood quorums, Relief Society and Young Women classes.(The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints) Starting in September, this will be the Sunday worship schedule for the global faith.“In the new schedule, sacrament meeting will continue to be no longer than 60 minutes,” the church’s governing First Presidency wrote in a letter to leaders and members. “... We are confident that members will be blessed by these changes.”As in the past, Sunday school and Primary classes will study the scriptures using “Come, Follow Me — For Home and Church,” the church-produced study guide. A news release explained that elders quorums (for men) and women’s Relief Society classes will continue “to study messages from the most recent General Conference.”“Gathering weekly in every class helps deepen gospel learning by connecting it more closely to personal and family study,” Paul V. Johnson, general president of the Sunday school, said in the release. “It also enhances the spiritual support that members get. Though the schedule looks different, the amount of time spent learning together remains the same.”Report AdYoung people between ages 11 and 18, “will use a new and expanded edition of ‘For the Strength of Youth: A Guide for Making Choices,’ supported by material available in church magazines,” according to the updated schedule. That revised guide “features 12 chapters that align with monthly study.”(The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints) An updated “For the Strength of Youth: A Guide for Making Choices” features 12 chapters that align with monthly study. Beginning Sept. 6, this guide will become the curriculum for Young Women classes and Aaronic Priesthood quorums.It will “become the curriculum for Young Women classes and Aaronic Priesthood quorums,” the church said. “Additional supporting content will be provided through the ‘For the Strength of Youth’ magazine, starting with the September 2026 issue.”The guide “is simple but powerful. It will help young men and young women focus on Christ, know his doctrine, and listen to the Spirit,” said Timothy L. Farnes, Young Men general president. “This guide will help youth walk in confidence, rely on his power, and move forward with hope in a challenging world.”
